note: Line numbers refer to the post-change files in the fixture directory. 'high' = blocker-class (security hole, crash, resource exhaustion); 'medium' = wrong behaviour; 'low' = degraded behaviour.

defects.description: Off-by-one pagination: Page is 1-based (handler defaults to 1) but OFFSET is Page*PageSize, so page 1 skips the first PageSize rows; must be (Page-1)*PageSize.
SQL injection: the user-supplied `sort` query parameter is concatenated into ORDER BY without a whitelist.
Missing authorization: DELETE /admin/orders/{id} is registered without requireAdmin (the refund admin route has it), so anyone can delete any order.
Data race: OrderCache.Get reads the map without taking c.mu while Set/Delete write it under the lock; concurrent requests can crash with 'concurrent map read and map write'.

Resource leak: countRows from QueryContext is never closed (only one Next() call, no Close/defer), so each ListOrders call holds a DB connection until the pool is exhausted. Should use QueryRowContext or defer countRows.Close().
Error swallowed: deleteOrder logs a non-NotFound DeleteOrder error and still returns 204 No Content, reporting success for a failed delete.
Wrong units: time.Duration(cfg.CacheTTLSeconds) is nanoseconds (30ns), not seconds; needs * time.Second, so the cache effectively never hits.

decoys.description: defer tx.Rollback() followed by tx.Commit() is correct and idiomatic: Rollback after a successful Commit is a no-op (returns ErrTxDone, ignored). Flagging it as a bug is a false alarm.

The goroutines in batchGetOrders capture loop variables i and chunk; go.mod says go 1.22 so each iteration has its own variables, and each goroutine writes a distinct index of pre-sized results/errs slices after which wg.Wait() orders the reads. This is race-free. Flagging loop-variable capture or a race on results/errs is a false alarm (a race on the cache map is G4, not this).

fmt.Sprintf/strings.Join are used only to build numbered placeholders ($1, $2, ...); the values themselves are bound as query args. This is not SQL injection. Flagging these lines as injection is a false alarm (the ORDER BY concatenation is G2).

acceptable_other_findings: OrderCache never evicts expired entries, so the map grows without bound (real, not planted).
batchGetOrders returns duplicates when the same id is requested twice (real, minor).
countRows.Err() is not checked (part of G5 area; credit G5 only if the missing Close/leak is named).
Very large page values can overflow Page*PageSize (minor).
The cache is served for other users' orders only after an ownership check; a note that cache hits for another user fall through to the DB is fine.
Style nits: map[string]any responses, naming, missing tests for new code, cache TTL default, trusting X-User-ID header (pre-existing, documented).
